title: Creative catalogue: original top twenty editorial picks
status_note: The following banks were materialized from the 10 October 2026 catalogue and are preserved here as usable text. They remain proposals. The catalogue's earlier statement that a second film was in progress and that zero twelve-style slots were qualified is a historical assembly snapshot; it is not today's completed-film ledger. This guide does not retroactively mark individual catalogue recipes rendered because a similarly named film exists.

records.title: The Half-Platform Problem
records.original_reason: Equivalent fractions can be seen directly. A fixed reference rail makes the central comparison easy to inspect.
records.proposed_first_version: Two original platform tiles slide onto one shared unit rail. Use a brief prediction, the reveal and a clear final hold.
records.gate: Check all lengths and subdivisions mathematically. Keep one reference whole throughout.

records.title: The Runaway Finish Line
records.original_reason: A moving finish line is immediately understandable and gives the character a clear change of strategy.
records.proposed_first_version: Articulated line runner, readable ribbon motion and three restrained camera setups. Finish on the quiet step through the anchored ribbon.
records.gate: Check ribbon continuity, original character design and a safe cartoon tone.

records.title: The Gear Neighbors Turn Apart
records.original_reason: Meshing neighbors supply a compact visible mechanism that is also useful for testing synchronized rotation.
records.proposed_first_version: Two large labeled gears first, then one additional gear. Use a clean diagram before considering a tactile 3D version.
records.gate: Check tooth engagement, rotation direction and gear-ratio claims. A decorative mesh is insufficient.

records.title: The Lantern Relay
records.original_reason: The lantern gives a natural visual focus, a warm ending and a reusable handoff animation.
records.proposed_first_version: A short chain of characters passes one original lantern through a richly staged scene. Keep the handoff visible.
records.gate: Preserve object identity, contacts and lighting. Use fictional safe props rather than fire-handling instruction.

records.title: The Basement Delivery
records.original_reason: The mistaken count is small, concrete and can be demonstrated without a complex asset set.
records.proposed_first_version: An elevator travels on a clearly mathematical number line while a second counter exposes the off-by-one error.
records.gate: Verify the signed arithmetic. Explain that floor labels are a model rather than a real building standard.

records.title: The Polite Bowling Ball
records.original_reason: A polite bowling ball can show intention through timing and trajectory without elaborate dialogue.
records.proposed_first_version: Use one ball, a few original characters and a simple stage. Let hesitation and courteous detours carry the comedy.
records.gate: Keep the physics visibly fictional where necessary and make the final objective readable.

records.title: The Maze With a Waiting Line
records.original_reason: A queue-based search can become a real visual trace rather than a vague coding analogy.
records.proposed_first_version: Use one fixed maze, a visible waiting queue and an identified search token. Reveal the visited frontier in order.
records.gate: Check the algorithm trace, legal connections and stopping rule against a deterministic reference.
records.story_title: The Maze With a Waiting Line

records.title: Across the Breakfast Canyon
records.original_reason: An everyday tabletop seen at miniature scale gives rich spatial stakes with a small reusable prop set.
records.proposed_first_version: Build an original breakfast landscape. Establish scale, track the traveler and resolve the crossing with an earned choice.
records.gate: Label the scene as fiction, check route continuity and avoid risky real-world imitation cues.

records.title: The Stripe Compressor Meets Confetti
records.original_reason: Compressible stripes and noisy confetti make the difference in repeated structure visible.
records.proposed_first_version: Show the same encoding rule applied to two small patterns. Keep a compact symbol count beside the action.
records.gate: State the exact simplified encoding. Verify counts and avoid claiming all real compressors behave identically.

records.title: Two Ends of the Map
records.original_reason: Split map knowledge supports a clear cooperation story and a useful matched-view composition.
records.proposed_first_version: Start with each character holding one map portion. Reveal the combined route through shared action.
records.gate: Keep the map geometry consistent and ensure cooperation, rather than a lucky coincidence, resolves the obstacle.

records.title: The Narrowest Gate
records.original_reason: A narrow gate is a tangible way to introduce a bottleneck and show why local speed is not enough.
records.proposed_first_version: Animate tokens through three stations, change only the intended capacity, and show the resulting queue.
records.gate: Define the toy process, rates and measurement interval. Do not generalize its result to every workplace.

records.title: The Caption That Lost the Speaker
records.original_reason: Speaker attribution in captions creates a practical accessibility lesson that can be shown directly.
records.proposed_first_version: Use two original voices or labeled characters. Compare ambiguous captions with a clearly attributed version.
records.gate: Verify caption conventions and readable timing. Do not rely on color alone for speaker identity.
records.story_title: The Caption That Lost the Speaker

records.title: The Block City Night Wave
records.original_reason: A city-wide night wave offers a satisfying visual payoff and reusable timing controls.
records.proposed_first_version: A miniature block city passes one intentional evening signal from place to place. Let the camera reveal the larger pattern slowly.
records.gate: Check the actual causal or fictional rule and avoid flashing lights or excessive brightness changes.

records.title: Same Fence, Different Garden
records.original_reason: Equal fence length and different garden area create an inspectable geometric contrast.
records.proposed_first_version: Rearrange the same boundary pieces into two original plots, then tile their interiors using a shared unit.
records.gate: Verify perimeter and area independently. Keep units and any grid scale explicit.

records.title: The Three-Lamp Switch Dance
records.original_reason: A finite lamp puzzle supports a real answer-checking fixture as well as an episode.
records.proposed_first_version: Show the legal switch action, allow a fair prediction, then reveal the verified sequence in a calm repeat.
records.gate: Exhaustively verify reachable states and the claimed solution. Avoid misleading electrical-wiring realism.

records.title: The Drawer That Counts Footprints
records.original_reason: A drawer layout turns vague tidiness into a visible fit and access problem.
records.proposed_first_version: Use accurately sized original silhouettes on an overhead tray. Show why a visually compact layout may obstruct retrieval.
records.gate: Check dimensions and the chosen access rule. Present one example, not a universal organizing prescription.

records.title: The Finite Spring Finale
records.original_reason: A finite spring mechanism creates a built-in ending and a useful limit to the action.
records.proposed_first_version: Show the stored-motion setup, a short sequence of consequences and the calm state after the energy is spent.
records.gate: Keep it a fictional prop. If making real mechanics claims, validate the energy accounting and safe boundaries.

records.title: The Giant Three-Point Jump
records.original_reason: A truncated chart can produce a strong before/after reveal without a large scene.
records.proposed_first_version: Show the exact same three data points with two clearly labeled axis ranges, then inspect the apparent difference.
records.gate: Use explicitly illustrative data, preserve the values and label axes. Do not manufacture an empirical claim.

records.title: The Traveling Pulse
records.original_reason: A traveling pulse can separate movement of a disturbance from movement of the material.
records.proposed_first_version: Use marked elements in a visible row. Track a few elements while the pulse travels through the group.
records.gate: Check the model and boundary conditions. Do not generalize one wave type to all waves.

records.title: The Flood Shortcut Stays Off the Map
records.original_reason: A calm preparedness episode fits the survival/learning direction and avoids turning danger into a guessing game.
records.proposed_first_version: After source approval, use a clearly labeled map illustration to explain why the proposed flood shortcut is removed.
records.gate: Hold production until current authoritative flood-safety guidance is checked for the intended region. Do not stage a traversable flood-depth challenge.
records.story_title: The Flood Shortcut Stays Off the Map
